audit_findings.title: Convertible-note treatment mixes debt and equity claims
audit_findings.magnitude: 28.308 million gross note shares versus 8.528 million conversion-spread shares at $110.19; 19.780 million excess shares. Removing them reduces the denominator from 151.404 million to 131.624 million and raises per-share values about 15.0% before capped-call offsets
audit_findings.mechanism: The error enters the fully diluted share denominator and claim bridge: principal is cash-settled, so only the conversion spread is an equity claim, while capped calls offset additional dilution.
audit_findings.evidence: Since we have committed to settle the principal amount of the Convertible Notes in cash upon conversion only, the number of shares for the conversion spread will be included as a dilutive common stock equivalent.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated denominator error, not merely a possibility. A spread-only denominator would move bear/base/bull values from $57.43/$67.55/$79.43 to approximately $66.06/$77.70/$91.37 before capped-call benefits. Although those values remain below the $110.19 market price, the roughly 15% change is material to stated intrinsic value and the capped-call effect remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild the claim bridge for each note using conversion-spread shares at the valuation price, apply each outstanding capped call through its contractual cap, reconcile to the 151.404 million denominator, and rerun only per-share values and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: Perpetual growth may cross a material royalty-rate cliff
audit_findings.magnitude: $867.840 million of 2025 royalties, including $745.492 million from DARZALEX, VYVGART Hytrulo and Phesgo; terminal value is 47.7%-51.5% of operating PV; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Patent-linked royalty-rate reductions would lower future owner earnings and invalidate the modeled fade to 2.5% perpetual growth, particularly in the terminal-value period.
audit_findings.evidence: In general, when there are no valid claims of a specified patent developed under the collaboration covering the product in a given country, the royalty rate is reduced for those sales in that country upon the expiration of our patents covering rHuPH20.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual step-down mechanism and 2027-2029 rHuPH20 patent expirations are demonstrated, but the affected country-product sales and post-expiry rates are not supplied. Because royalties represent 62.1% of 2025 revenue and roughly half of operating value comes from the terminal period, even a partial cliff is reasonably capable of materially reducing value.
audit_findings.action: Map each material product-country royalty stream to valid product-specific claims, contractual royalty term, step-down date and post-expiry rate, then rerun all scenarios with explicit DARZALEX, VYVGART Hytrulo, Phesgo and other-principal-stream cliffs.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $23.0 million Elektrofi contingent liability plus up to $100.0 million Surf Bio contingent consideration; $123.0 million maximum equals $0.81 per share and 1.0%-1.4% of scenario equity values
audit_findings.mechanism: Contingent acquisition payments are senior cash claims that should enter the equity bridge or normalized acquisition reinvestment rather than remain outside both owner earnings and the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The $ 100.0 million in contingent consideration will be recognized in the future when and if milestones are met (i.e., when the contingent consideration is paid or payable) and does not meet the definition of a derivative.
audit_findings.explanation: The $23.0 million Elektrofi amount is recognized and the additional Surf Bio payment is contingent and not yet payable. Even deducting the full disclosed $123.0 million would reduce base value from $67.55 to about $66.74 per share and the buy-below price by about $0.57, while leaving the market price above the bull value. That concrete maximum scale is not material to the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the June 2026 carrying value and milestone status of both obligations; deduct any payable or probability-weighted claim consistently in the bridge, but no full valuation redesign is required unless consideration exceeds the disclosed $123.0 million.

audit_findings.title: Recurring acquisition investment may have been treated as a free one-off
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,013.736 million of FY2025 acquisition cash outlays; amounts requiring normalization review include $284.887 million acquired IPR&D, $48.700 million impairment and $23.9 million of disclosed transaction expenses
audit_findings.mechanism: Reversing acquisition-related charges increases anchor owner earnings, while excluding recurring acquisition cash investment allows modeled growth without the reinvestment required to obtain or replace acquired technologies.
audit_findings.evidence: In order to augment and extend our revenue, we acquired Antares (in May 2022), Elektrofi (in November 2025), and Surf Bio (in December 2025) and we may decide to acquire additional businesses, products and technologies or pursue other corporate transactions and make investments which we believe are important to the future of our business.
audit_findings.explanation: The acquisition spending and reversed-charge candidates are demonstrated, but recurrence is not. FY2025 acquisition cash exceeded the $711.5 million anchor, and the identified charges total $357.487 million, or 50.2% of the anchor. If acquisitions or replacement investment are necessary to sustain modeled growth, the omission is plainly capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Produce the complete $711.5 million anchor reconciliation, identify every acquisition-related add-back, and rerun scenarios with a normalized probability-weighted acquisition or technology-replacement reinvestment charge consistent with the growth credited.

audit_findings.title: Working-capital consumption may be absent from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $152.256 million computed FY2025 net operating working-capital cash use, equal to 21.4% of the $711.5 million anchor; $69.763 million computed net use in the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring increases in receivables, inventory, prepayments and operating liabilities reduce cash distributable to equity and therefore should reduce anchor and forecast owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in net cash provided by operations was primarily due to an increase in revenue, partially offset by higher working capital spend.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash absorption is demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show whether it was included in the owner-earnings reconciliation or how much was temporary or acquisition-related. The FY2025 amount is large enough relative to the anchor, and continued net use appears in the first half of 2026, so omission of the sustainable portion is reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile owner earnings to the cash-flow-statement working-capital lines, remove acquired balances and temporary timing items, estimate normalized working capital as a function of recurring revenue, and rerun all scenarios with that cash requirement.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor may capitalize lumpy milestone revenue
audit_findings.magnitude: $135.471 million of 2025 upfront, target-nomination, development, regulatory and sales-based milestone revenue, equal to 19.0% of the $711.5 million anchor; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Using a latest-year owner-earnings anchor without normalizing nonannual collaboration receipts can capitalize temporary revenue through the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect these revenues to continue to fluctuate in future periods based on our partners’ ability to meet various clinical, regulatory and event-based milestones set forth in such agreements and our ability to obtain new collaborative agreements.
audit_findings.explanation: The presence and fluctuation of milestone and upfront revenue are demonstrated, but an anchor error is not. The record does not provide the related taxes, costs, revenue recognized before occurrence, or a probability-weighted sustainable portfolio level. The gross revenue is potentially significant, but the available record cannot establish the net owner-earnings overstatement or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Disaggregate the anchor into royalties, product margins, device-development earnings, upfront fees and each milestone class; identify revenue recognized before milestone occurrence and replace nonrecurring components with a probability-weighted multiyear normalized amount before rerunning the valuation.
